label: At D1, update gate is high after reaching S2 last trial (most after a1), low after S1.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state > 0) * belief_lo
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 19 is active essentially only at D1 (GO/D2 near 0). Its D1 magnitude is set by the state reached on the previous trial: high (~+0.3 to +0.55 above timing) when last trial reached S2, low (~-0.38) when it reached S1; within S2, higher if it was reached by a1 (rare transition) than by a2 (common). Previous reward barely matters (r vs u differ by <0.08). The free fit adds small reward-at-S2 and belief_lo terms (dev 0.81 vs 0.79 for the short form); belief, trial-before and future cues add little. Not driven by observed-only belief beyond what the last state carries.

issues: The claims hold up. The short form scores test R^2 0.787 beyond timing. The 'last trial' reference table alone scores 0.79 and the all-observed ceiling is 0.81, so the short form is close to the observable ceiling.
The residual tables confirm 'only at D1': GO and D2 residuals are all below 0.02 in size. At D1 the residual is +0.55 after a1-S2, +0.28 to +0.36 after a2-S2 and about -0.38 after S1.

The third term is not unique. Replacing (prev_action == 1) with (prev_common == 0) inside S2 gives the same fit (0.787), because a1->S2 is by definition the rare transition. Replacing it with (prev_state == 2) * belief_lo also ties at 0.788, with a positive weight: higher when belief favours S1. So 'most after a1' could equally be read as 'most when S2 was unexpected'; the label's wording is still accurate.

Reward claim checked: swapping in (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) gives 0.767, below the action term. Reward does matter a little after a2-S2 (r +0.28 vs u +0.36), which slightly undercuts 'barely matters', but the gap stays under 0.08 as stated.

Misses show no large systematic error class. The worst cell is D1 after a2-S2-unrewarded at +0.059. Many of the worst windows are the first D1 of a window, where the previous trial is unknown, plus a2-S2 trials where z reaches about 0.95 against a prediction of about 0.65. The activation looks close to binary (about 0 or about 0.95), so the leftover variance probably comes from all-or-none firing within a cell, which these additive cues do not capture.
